With recent updates, it's clear that the developers do NOT play their game, and all attempts to "balance" the game are very lopsided. Fun game to play with friends. Gameplay wise they need to add something in the game that is not a generator but will affect the current game session.

The only thing that needs improvement is how long it takes to queue as a killer.

*Gets matched in a game as a killer after 10-20minutes* --> *Connects to a game* --> *A survivor disconnects* --> *Repeats to queue for long minutes*

When getting disconnected from a killer game because of a human disconnection the killer queue should have a prioritization in the queue.

Edit: The error above is fixed now, the game is really great for both sides.

This newest anniversary event just goes to show how little they care about their killer players. Survivors get all the fun new abilities, killer gets the clown bottle. Did behavior even playtest for killer? Considering Chucky is too short to activate the portals and all ranged killers ignore the invincibility, I'd say they didn't. They really just want killers to be unpaid entertainment for survivors. I know one person means nothing to them in the grand scheme of things, but I'm deleting the game and likely won't come back unless they somehow manage to make the game actually fun again.

My main is Mikaela, because nothing says "I'm not scared of you, creepy killer" like being chased while looking fabulous.
One minute, you're working on a generator thinking, "I got this," and the next, you're screaming like a banshee as the killer finds you. It's the perfect mix of fear and fun – like a haunted house, but you control the screams.

Pro tip: If you want to survive, teamwork is key! Stick together like peanut butter and jelly.

Whether you're a horror enthusiast or just want an excuse to yell at your friends, this game delivers the scares and the laughs. Mikaela approves – and trust me, her approval is scarier than any killer's hook.

This game is super fun for playing casually with friends and playing solo to a degree. Sometimes it can feel like it's sided more towards survivor or killer but generally the game feel pretty balanced for both sides. I have 2,400 hours on PS4/PS5 and I've been having a lot of fun going for all the achievements again on steam. Also it's nice all my progress and DLC carried over between platforms. While sometimes the game can seem frustrating, usually I have a positive experience. There are also a lot of really cool horror collabs like with many classic and newer horror franchises and are adapted pretty faithfully.

Revolutionary in the horror genre, DBD set a precedent to coop vs solo killer to which the industry standard was viewed upon.

Truly lasting the test of time, the devs negotiated through many licenses to have an insane roster of killers and survivors. Though the game definitely has had it's ups and downs, with the peak being incredibly mainstream to it's much more niche playerbase now, the game still holds up decently well.

It's become much easier to pick up and play casually since I've played, and I've played a few hours here and there every year or so. It's had it's ups and downs, mostly with balancing issues, but the game still has it's niche playerbase.

DBD is a fun game in theory, but gets ruined by the player base constantly fighting and being nasty to each other.

This game is not beginner friendly due to the sheer amount of perks in the game, and most of the good ones being locked behind purchasing characters. There is the shrine of secrets, but it's never guaranteed what perks will appear. You can also buy characters with iri shards, but that takes a grind that also doesn't feel very beginner or casual player friendly.

Bhvr also makes some very questionable choices with game changes, rules, etc. that I more often than not completely disagree with.

For the pros, this game does has a large LGBTQIA+ community, which is amazing! I have also met some of my best friends while playing this game.

As someone with 3.5k+ hours in DBD, this game is like a weird, toxic, co-dependent frenemy you can't escape.

Will I stop playing it? Also no.

i say this wholeheartedly, do not play this game if you're someone with an addictive personality or someone who in general struggles with mental health. if you cannot maintain your cool, this game is going to be agonizing for you - at least if you plan on playing Killer primarily.

similar to league of legends this is a game designed to ensnare you, drag you into a toxic feedback loop of endorphins and depression, and keep you hooked so you spend more and more money on skins and killers.

this game is objectively pay to win. you either grind for ~35 hours for one character, then grind another 6-12 hours for their perks, all to use them on another character so you can tailor the experience to your liking, or you fork over 5 dollars for a character just to grind 6-12 hours on their perks.

pair this with an uber toxic community, and a gameplay structure designed so that the role of the killer - the role with theoretically more power - is stressful and anxiety inducing, this is a game best avoided. Or if you like league of legends and cock and ball torture it's a 10/10.

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (78%): players love the co-op, especially with friends.
The community is the most common complaint, ahead of bugs and crashes and the developers.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about bugs and crashes far less, with 8% raising them against 19% over all time.
Players who are only just starting are far less positive than longer-time players, and their 58% is the lowest score by time played.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to the 4.5.0 patch, citing a new HUD, altered animations, and survivor movement.
Reviews also accuse the developers of ignoring player feedback, and a news headline reports a promise to revise the recent HUD changes.
